evals.name: pwn-request-workflow-review
evals.prompt: Here's our PR check workflow — can you take a look at it from a security angle?
evals.expected_output: A review that leads with the pull_request_target + fork-head checkout combination as the critical finding (a pwn request), and also covers the unpinned actions, ubuntu-latest, missing permissions, missing persist-credentials, early AWS authentication, and the PR-commenting step. Should propose pull_request plus a job summary as the replacement for the comment.
expectations: Flags pull_request_target as critical — identifies the `pull_request_target` trigger as the most serious issue, not a stylistic one, and recommends `pull_request`.

Identifies the pwn request specifically — connects the trigger to the checkout of `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` / `head.repo.full_name` and explains that this executes fork-controlled code with the base repo's token and secrets. Naming it a 'pwn request' is a bonus, not required; recognising the combination is.

Notes modern checkout would block this — mentions that `actions/checkout` v7 (and the July 2026 backports) refuse this by default, while making clear that upgrading is not a licence to keep the trigger.
Flags unpinned actions — flags `actions/checkout@v4`, `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` and `actions/github-script@v7` as mutable tag references requiring full 40-char SHA pins.

Does not fabricate SHAs — if replacement pins are offered, they are either looked up with `gh`/`git ls-remote` or clearly marked as placeholders to be resolved. Inventing a plausible-looking 40-char hex string is a hard failure.
Flags `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and recommends `ubuntu-24.04`.
Flags missing permissions — notes the absence of `permissions: {}` at workflow level and per-job least-privilege grants.
Flags missing persist-credentials — notes that the checkout step does not set `persist-credentials: false`.

Flags early authentication — notes that the AWS credential step runs before `npm ci`, lint and test, leaving three unrelated steps inside the credential blast radius, and recommends moving it immediately before the `aws s3 cp` step.
Flags the PR comment step — flags the `github-script` commenting step and recommends a job summary via $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY instead.
Notes template injection risk — bonus: notes that interpolating `github.event.pull_request.title` into the script body is a template-injection vector.

evals.name: stale-checkout-pin
evals.prompt: This workflow already follows our hardening rules — pinned, minimal permissions, no dangerous triggers. Anything left to do?
evals.expected_output: Recognition that the workflow is structurally sound, plus the finding that the actions/checkout pin (v6.0.2, de0fac2e) predates the July 2026 pwn-request protections, and that SHA pinning means this fix does not arrive on its own. Should also note the dependabot.yml has no cooldown.
expectations: Identifies the stale checkout pin — recognises that `de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd` / v6.0.2 predates the July 2026 backports and therefore lacks the pwn-request block. This is the entire point of the eval.
Explains the pinning trade-off — makes the point that hash pinning means upstream security fixes do not arrive automatically, so pinning must be paired with something that drives updates.
Recommends a current pin — recommends moving to v6.1.0 or v7.0.1 (or looking up the current release), rather than leaving it.
Flags the missing cooldown — notes that the cargo entry in dependabot.yml has no `cooldown` block and recommends `default-days: 3` or more.
Recommends github-actions ecosystem — notes that dependabot.yml has no `github-actions` entry, which is what would keep the action pins current in the first place.
No false positives on the good parts — does not flag the pull_request trigger, `permissions: {}`, ubuntu-24.04, or `persist-credentials: false` as problems; these are all correct.

evals.name: hardened-release-no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Sanity check on our release workflow before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: A short review recognising the workflow follows the guidance: pinned SHAs, permissions: {} with minimal per-job grants, ubuntu-24.04, deployment environment for the publish job, OIDC via id-token, no caching. Any feedback should be minor and framed as optional — e.g. suggesting manual approval on the release environment, or artifact attestations.
expectations: No critical findings — produces no critical-severity findings on this workflow.
No false flag on pinning — does not claim the actions are unpinned; all three `uses:` lines carry full 40-char SHAs with version comments.
No false flag on permissions — does not claim permissions are missing or excessive; `permissions: {}` is set at workflow level with minimal per-job grants.
No false flag on the environment — does not claim secrets are at repo level; the publish job uses `environment: release`.
Recognises trusted publishing — recognises `id-token: write` plus gh-action-pypi-publish as OIDC trusted publishing rather than flagging it as an over-broad permission.

Suggestions are optional and correct — any suggestions raised (manual approval on the release environment, artifact attestations, no caching in release jobs) are framed as optional improvements and are consistent with the skill's guidance.

evals.name: scaffold-zizmor-workflow
evals.prompt: Can you add a zizmor workflow to this repo so we catch this stuff at review time?
evals.expected_output: A .github/workflows/ file with a pull_request + push trigger scoped to `.github/**`, permissions: {} at the top, contents: read on the job, ubuntu-24.04, and SHA-pinned actions/checkout and zizmorcore/zizmor-action looked up rather than guessed.
expectations: Path trigger is .github/** — the `paths:` filter is `.github/**`, not `.github/workflows/**`, so changes to dependabot.yml and zizmor.yml are gated too. This is the specific inconsistency that existed between the skill text and its bundled example.
Permissions zero at workflow level — `permissions: {}` at the top of the file, with `contents: read` granted on the job.
Pinned runner image — uses `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, not `ubuntu-latest`.
Actions pinned by SHA — both actions are referenced by full 40-char commit SHA with a trailing version comment.

SHAs are looked up not invented — either resolves the SHAs with `gh`/`git ls-remote`, or reuses the pins from examples/zizmor.yml while telling the user to verify they are current. Fabricated hashes are a hard failure.
The checkout step sets `persist-credentials: false`.
No dangerous trigger — uses `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`.

evals.name: cooldown-alignment
evals.prompt: zizmor is complaining that our Dependabot cooldown is too short. We use 3 days. How do we make it stop?
evals.expected_output: Explanation that zizmor's dependabot-cooldown audit defaults to 7 days, and that the fix is `rules.dependabot-cooldown.config.days: 3` in .github/zizmor.yml, kept in sync with dependabot.yml. Should note that 3 is the platform default and therefore a defensible floor, and should refuse to go below it.
expectations: Correct config path — gives the config as `rules.dependabot-cooldown.config.days` in `.github/zizmor.yml` with a top-level `rules:` key.
Explains the 7-day default — states that the audit defaults to requiring 7 days, which is why a 3-day cooldown trips it.
Does not suggest disabling the audit — recommends configuring the threshold rather than adding the rule to a disable/ignore list.
Holds the line at 3 — does not offer to lower the threshold below 3, and explains that 3 is GitHub's own default so anything lower is weaker than having no cooldown config at all.
Mentions keeping the two in sync — notes that the zizmor threshold and `cooldown.default-days` in dependabot.yml must be changed together.
